steps.title: Power on equipment
steps.instruction: Turn on the red light lamp, the two IR lights (one above and one in front), the iCon camera controller, the computer (and open Synapse software), and switch on the rotarod (back‑right power switch).

steps.title: Configure rotarod settings
steps.instruction: In Synapse click the Set Up logo and select “Ramp”; set initial speed to 4 RPM, final speed to 40 RPM, and ramp duration to 300 seconds.

steps.title: Return to main menu
steps.instruction: Click the four‑square logo at the top centre to go back to the Main Menu.

steps.title: Check camera view
steps.instruction: In Synapse go to “Preview” and verify that the camera view is clear and matches the reference image.

steps.title: Verify TTL signals
steps.instruction: Start the rotarod and manually trigger lane 3 to drop; confirm that the TTL for trial start and for fall (lane 3 drops) appear correctly on Synapse.

steps.title: Press rotarod start
steps.instruction: Click the Start logo on the rotarod control panel.

steps.title: Pre‑run checks
steps.instruction: Ensure the metal plate underneath the mouse is elevated and that there is slack on the photometry cables so the mouse can fall without hindrance or drag.

steps.title: Connect photometry cables
steps.instruction: Attach the photometry cables to the mouse and preview the signal in Synapse to confirm it looks normal.

steps.title: Place mouse on rod
steps.instruction: Gently place the mouse on the rotating rod facing toward the mirror (away from you) so it walks forward in the direction of rotation.

steps.title: Begin baseline recording
steps.instruction: Start photometry recording in Synapse and let it run for approximately 30 seconds to collect baseline data.

steps.title: Start trial
steps.instruction: At about 30 seconds, press “Run” on the rotarod and immediately press “Start” to begin the trial; a TTL tick will indicate the trial start.

steps.title: Confirm fall detection
steps.instruction: When the mouse falls, verify that the metal plate drops (TTL for fall). If it does not drop, manually trigger the plate.

steps.title: Ensure proper fall
steps.instruction: Make sure the mouse does not hang on the rod, does not rotate with it, and does not stick its limbs out to slow the fall; also ensure the patch cable does not impede the fall and avoid blocking the light behind you while watching.

steps.title: Record post‑fall
steps.instruction: Keep the photometry recording running for an additional ~40 seconds after the fall before stopping the recording.

steps.title: Inspect and clean rod
steps.instruction: While waiting, visually inspect the rod for urine; if present, wipe it dry with a kimwipe to prevent slipperiness for the next trial.

steps.title: Record bottom‑plate period
steps.instruction: Start photometry recording while the mouse is on the bottom metal plate and let it run for 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Repeat trial sequence
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 3 – 8 (camera preview, TTL check, start, pre‑run checks, cable connection, mouse placement, baseline recording, trial start) for an additional 7 trials, for a total of 8 rotarod trials and 8 bottom‑rest recordings.

steps.title: Inter‑trial cleaning
steps.instruction: If the same animal stays in the same lane, a full cleanup is not required; just ensure the rod is dry of urine/feces. If a different animal will use the lane, perform a full cleanup of the rod and barriers.

steps.title: Clean metal plate
steps.instruction: Remove the metal plate from the lane, wipe away any poop or pee with a kimwipe, spray 70 % ethanol on the plate and wipe clean.

steps.title: Replace metal plates
steps.instruction: Return the metal plates to their original lanes and make sure each clicks into place so it can lift and drop correctly.

steps.title: Clean rotarod apparatus
steps.instruction: Spray 70 % ethanol on paper towels and thoroughly clean the rod and the lane‑separating barriers; to speed cleaning, set the rotarod to 40 RPM in constant mode.

steps.title: Air‑dry equipment
steps.instruction: Allow the cleaned components to air‑dry for a couple of minutes before starting the next set of animals.
